candidate_relations.label: Cavernous Angioma, left tentorial extra-axial
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record explicitly notes that cavernous angioma was only a pre-operative radiologic suggestion. Histopathology demonstrated high mitotic activity (up to 20/10 HPF), spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature, and IHC positivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1 with CD34 negativity — a profile consistent with angiosarcoma, not cavernous angioma. Cavernous angioma is a benign, non-neoplastic vascular malformation with no mitotic activity and no malignant histologic features, making it an incompatible subtype relative to the reference diagnosis of angiosarcoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Cavernous angioma is a benign vascular malformation; angiosarcoma is a malignant vascular neoplasm — same anatomical region but fundamentally incompatible diagnostic entity/subtype

case_quality_flags: Pre-operative imaging misled toward cavernous angioma; histopathology is definitive for malignant vascular neoplasm
CD34 negativity in an angiosarcoma is atypical but reported; high mitotic index and CD31/Fli-1 positivity support angiosarcoma over epithelioid hemangioendothelioma or other vascular tumors
